Targeting C0001 as a qualified baseline is unsupported by the text.

judgments.rationale: 49 CFR 392.10(a) establishes a mandatory stopping duty before crossing railroad tracks at grade, explicitly conditioned by '[e]xcept as provided in paragraph (b) of this section.' Paragraph (b)(1) specifies that a stop need not be made at a streetcar crossing or industrial switching tracks within a business district. Setting relation to 'exception' and qualifying C0000 accurately converts this prose caveat into an explicit qualification edge targeting the stopping duty baseline while preserving the correct 'not_required' modality.

Paragraph (a) establishes the stopping requirement before crossing railroad tracks subject to the exceptions in paragraph (b). Paragraph (b)(2) explicitly exempts drivers from stopping at a grade crossing when directed to proceed by a police officer or crossing flagman. Updating C0010 to have an 'exception' relation qualifying baseline claim C0000 faithfully reflects this statutory exception and preserves the appropriate 'not_required' modality.

Paragraph (a) imposes the railroad crossing stop requirement except as provided in paragraph (b). Paragraph (b)(3) exempts crossings controlled by a functioning highway traffic signal showing a green indication permitting crossing without stopping or slowing under local law. Linking C0011 to baseline C0000 as an 'exception' accurately models this qualification edge while maintaining the proper 'not_required' modal force.

Paragraph (a) establishes the baseline railroad crossing stop duty subject to paragraph (b), and paragraph (b)(4) specifies that a stop need not be made at an abandoned railroad grade crossing marked with an abandoned rail line sign. Changing C0012's relation to 'exception' qualifying C0000 correctly establishes the structural link to the duty it qualifies while retaining the 'not_required' modality.

Paragraph (a) mandates stopping at grade crossings except as provided in paragraph (b), and paragraph (b)(5) explicitly provides that a stop need not be made at an industrial or spur line grade crossing marked with an 'Exempt' sign. Structuring C0013 as an 'exception' qualifying C0000 accurately captures the relationship to the stopping baseline and preserves the 'not_required' modality.

source_spans.quote: (a) Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, the driver of a commercial motor vehicle specified in paragraphs (a) (1) through (6) of this section shall not cross a railroad track or tracks at grade unless he/she first: Stops the commercial motor vehicle within 50 feet of, and not closer than 15 feet to, the tracks; thereafter listens and looks in each direction along the tracks for an approaching train; and ascertains that no train is approaching. When it is safe to do so, the driver may drive the commercial motor vehicle across the tracks in a gear that permits the commercial motor vehicle to complete the crossing without a change of gears. The driver must not shift gears while crossing the tracks.

(b) A stop need not be made at:

(1) A streetcar crossing, or railroad tracks used exclusively for industrial switching purposes, within a business district, as defined in § 390.5 of this chapter.
